findings.claim: The plan says the briefing is read-only and leaves every store file's bytes as they were, but every existing reader it would reuse opens `Store`, and `Store.__init__` writes. It creates `.kmaudit/` and its `.gitignore`, copies `.kmctl/audit.sqlite` into `.kmaudit/.okf.sqlite` when that copy is missing, runs schema migrations, and inserts the `meta` namespace row. That covers `list_checks`, `list_claims`, `claim_row`, and the spike's own probe, whose 0.51s 'first open' was that copy. In this repository, the plan's own acceptance case, there is no `.kmaudit/` at all: the only store is the legacy file, at user_version 5, with no `meta` table. So the briefing must open store files itself with `mode=ro` (falling back to the legacy file, as `namespaces.listing` already does). It must read a store at an older schema without migrating it, and tolerate missing tables. And it must reuse `status_row`/`check`/`latest` (which take a `Store`) through a read-only handle rather than through `list_checks`. The plan names none of this, and the obvious build (call `list_checks` per namespace, as the spike did) breaks O1 and r2 on the first run against this repo. Also, the acceptance step of running `kmaudit checks list` to compare counts makes the very copy the briefing must not make, so the order of that check matters.

r1 and O1 say the pending-section count matches `kmaudit claims list`, but it can't in exactly the cases the plan cares about. `claims list` does not refresh, so it never sees a new or changed page (the r2 case). And `Store.documents` counts a section as extracted only when `e.key = s.key`, with no `previous_keys`, so on a store keyed under an earlier hash (the r3 case, and this repository's store today) `claims list` reports all 212 sections unextracted while the briefing must report them up to date. The contract should say pending comes from the cut-and-compare. Only sections stored, claims, check statuses and open feedback should be required to match the list verbs.
Read-only rested on Store, which writes on open.
Pending could not match claims list.

Opening a WAL-mode store with mode=ro creates -shm and -wal files beside it and leaves them after close, so the plan's read mechanism breaks its own acceptance and eval r2 (no file under .kmctl/ or .kmaudit/ appears). The legacy store and every Store-made store are WAL. The plan must pick a mechanism that leaves no sidecars (for example immutable=1, which skips locking and ignores a live -wal, so it can miss rows a running writer has not checkpointed) or narrow r2 to allow sidecars, and say which.
The briefing opened Store, whose constructor writes; it now reads store files itself and builds a read-only handle for status_row.
Pending could not match a list command; it is now the briefing's own count and eval r1 says so.
mode=ro on a WAL store leaves -wal/-shm sidecars; the plan, its acceptance case and eval r2 now allow them and check .sqlite bytes instead.

A store at any schema step before the feedback table (steps 1 to 4) makes the whole briefing print "unavailable", because status_row reads the checks and feedback tables with no fallback. The plan says the briefing reads whatever schema step the file is at and counts a missing table as empty.

The r1 test never stores feedback or a stored check, so the feedback count and the per-status counts are compared only in their trivial case (0 notes, every claim "no check"). A briefing that counted answered feedback, or always reported 0 notes, would pass.

commands.md and the --help epilog say the briefing prints nothing with no namespace, but with --json it prints {"namespaces": []}, and on an error --json prints the plain "unavailable" line, which is not JSON. The docs should say what --json prints in both cases.

entries.change: Each store is read read-only into an in-memory copy with SQLite's backup API and migrated there, so a store at any schema step briefs like a current one and the file is never written; the per-table fallback is gone.

A store rebuilt at each schema step 1 to 6 briefs with the same sections, claims and pending and an unchanged file (steps 1-4 fail on the old code); the counts test stores a holding check and a note, asserting holds, no check and 1 open note; the never-fails test checks --json prints an empty list and an unavailable key.
On an error, --json prints {namespaces: [], unavailable: REASON} instead of plain text; the help says what --json prints with no namespace and on an error.
The briefing section says older schema steps are read through a migrated in-memory copy, and what --json prints with no namespace and on an error.

findings.claim: the counts test did not store a check or feedback, so checks and feedback were never compared where they could differ
--json printed plain text on an error and the docs said 'nothing' for no namespace
